# nathanpotter.dev

[![CI](https://github.com/potterbotter/nathanpotter.dev/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/potterbotter/nathanpotter.dev/actions/workflows/ci.yml)

Personal site of Nathan Potter: an interactive HTML CV plus a portfolio of projects built with AI-assisted workflows.

**Live:** [nathanpotter.dev](https://nathanpotter.dev/?ref=github) · **Host:** Cloudflare Workers (static assets) · **Stack:** static HTML/CSS generated by a zero-dependency Node build script; a small Cloudflare Worker (Anthropic SDK, zod) serves the public APIs

Design principles, data and privacy: [DESIGN.md](DESIGN.md). Visual design and page specs: [design/handoff/](design/handoff/README.md).

## Structure

```
content/cv.json         ← all CV content: the single source of truth
build/build.mjs         ← generates dist/ from cv.json + templates
build/validate.mjs      ← content checks (duplicate IDs, unknown tags, broken view rules); the build fails on any
build/templates.mjs     ← HTML for every page (follows design/handoff)
build/flags.mjs         ← feature flags for unbuilt features
build/serve.mjs         ← local preview server
public/                 ← static files copied into dist/ as-is
  assets/css/tokens.css ← design tokens (copy of design/handoff/tokens/tokens.css)
  assets/css/site.css   ← components and layout
  assets/js/site.js     ← small enhancements; every page works without it
  assets/js/jobfit.js   ← the job-fit page: form, link fetch, streamed read
  _headers              ← security headers, including the Content-Security-Policy
src/worker.js           ← Worker: runs only for /api/* and /admin/* (static pages never reach it)
src/jobfit.js           ← job-fit prompt, output schema and the honesty checks
src/jobfit-api.js       ← job-fit endpoint: limits, budget, streaming
src/fetchjd.js          ← fetches a posting from a link (Greenhouse, Lever, Ashby, schema.org)
src/partialjson.js      ← streaming-JSON parser for the read as it arrives
src/analytics.js        ← cookieless first-party analytics: collection and retention
src/access.js           ← Cloudflare Access token verification
src/docx.js             ← dependency-free Word (.docx) writer
tests/                  ← node:test suite
migrations/             ← D1 schema for the public tables (analytics, job-fit runs, settings)
design/handoff/         ← Claude Design handoff: tokens, components, navigation, page specs
wrangler.jsonc          ← Cloudflare config: build, assets, Worker, D1, rate limits, vars
```

**Private tools:** `/admin/*` and `/api/admin/*` are passed through a service binding to a separate Worker in a private repo, which sits behind Cloudflare Access and verifies the Access token itself (see DESIGN.md, "Data and privacy"). Without that Worker those paths return 503, and the public site is unaffected.

**Analytics:** first-party, cookieless visit data collected by `site.js` → `/api/collect` → D1 (`src/analytics.js`). No IP addresses are stored; see DESIGN.md.

**Editing content:** change `content/cv.json`, then commit and push. Placeholder copy written as `[in brackets]` is hidden on the live site until it's replaced.

**Feature flags** in `build/flags.mjs` keep unbuilt features off public pages: `jobFitLive` (fit CTAs), `adminLive` (footer Admin link), `pdfLive` (PDF download), `turnstileSiteKey` (bot check on the job-fit form).

## Privacy guardrail (run once per clone)

Personal data lives in Cloudflare D1, never in this repo (see DESIGN.md, "Data and privacy"). Enable the pre-commit hook that blocks data-looking files:

```
git config core.hooksPath .githooks
```

## Local preview

With Node.js installed:

```
npm run preview
```

Then open http://localhost:8787. `npm run build:draft` builds with the `[placeholder]` copy visible.

The job-fit tool locally: create `.dev.vars` (git-ignored) with an `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` (or `DEV_FAKE_MODEL=true` for a canned read at no cost), run `npx wrangler d1 migrations apply nathanpotter-dev --local` once, then `npm run dev`. The same migration step creates the DPR calculator's preset table; without `TURNSTILE_SECRET` in `.dev.vars`, saves skip the bot check locally.

`npm test` runs the test suite: the job-fit honesty checks, Access token verification, the streaming parser, link fetching, the Word writer, the DPR engine and presets API, and the CSP hash. CI runs it and the build on every push and pull request.

## Deployment

Cloudflare Workers Builds is connected to this GitHub repo (Workers project `nathanpotter-dev`):

- Push to `main` → production deploy to https://nathanpotter.dev (about a minute). Cloudflare runs `npx wrangler deploy`, which runs the build command in `wrangler.jsonc` and uploads `dist/`.
- Push to any other branch → preview build with its own `*.workers.dev` preview URL. Those URLs send `noindex` headers.
- Dashboard build command: *(empty; the build lives in `wrangler.jsonc`)*. Deploy command: `npx wrangler deploy`.
- Secrets (`ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `TURNSTILE_SECRET`, `ADMIN_EMAIL`, `ALERT_EMAIL`) go in **Workers project → Settings → Variables and Secrets** as encrypted secrets, never in the repo. For local development they go in `.dev.vars` (git-ignored).

DNS and email are on Cloudflare too:

- `nathanpotter.dev` is attached to the Worker as a **Custom Domain**. Cloudflare creates the DNS record and certificate itself.
- `www.nathanpotter.dev` → proxied `AAAA 100::` placeholder record, plus a Redirect Rule (`https://www.*` → `https://${1}`, 301, query string preserved) sending it to the root domain.
- HTTPS: `.dev` is on the browser HSTS preload list, so HTTPS is mandatory. Cloudflare issues the certificate automatically. SSL/TLS mode is **Full (strict)** and **Always Use HTTPS** is on.
- Email: Cloudflare Email Routing receives `hello@nathanpotter.dev` (receive only).

## Decision log

| Date | Decision | Why |
|---|---|---|
| 2026-10-05 | Plain HTML/CSS, no framework or build step | The CV is a self-contained HTML file and the site is a few pages. Nothing to compile means nothing to break, and a framework can be added later if it's needed. |
| 2026-10-05 | Cloudflare over Vercel | Domain and DNS are already at Cloudflare, so custom domain and TLS take one click. Cloudflare can run the planned "ask me about my CV" endpoint with encrypted secrets, which removes Vercel's main advantage. |
| 2026-10-05 | Public GitHub repo `nathanpotter.dev` | The source and commit history are part of the portfolio, showing the workflow. No secrets live in the repo. |
| 2026-10-05 | Site lives in `public/` | Keeps the README and config out of the deployed site. |
| 2026-10-05 | Workers (static assets) instead of Pages | Cloudflare's dashboard routed Git imports to Workers, its recommended path for new projects. Same free static hosting, plus server-side code later goes in one Worker script. Required adding `wrangler.jsonc`. |
| 2026-10-05 | Root domain is canonical; `www` 301-redirects to it | One address to share and for search engines. `www` is handled by a Redirect Rule at Cloudflare's edge, not by the Worker. |
| 2026-10-05 | Always Use HTTPS on; Cloudflare-managed HSTS left off | `.dev` is already HSTS-preloaded in browsers. Always Use HTTPS covers non-browser clients, and Cloudflare's own HSTS setting adds risk for no gain. |
| 2026-10-05 | Design principles locked in `DESIGN.md` | One source of truth for the CV chat, Claude Design and coding sessions. Key ideas: skim first with depth on demand; AI output is always inspectable and correctable. |
| 2026-10-05 | Generic CV is the homepage; tools on their own pages | The PDF résumé links to the root domain, and recruiters skim for about 10 seconds. Tools are apps, not résumé content. |
| 2026-10-05 | Role views at paths (`/fintech/`, `/builder/`, `/climate/`) | Optimised for sending tailored links to recruiters. |
| 2026-10-05 | Public contact is `hello@` plus LinkedIn, no phone | Keeps personal details away from scrapers. The phone number stays on the PDF. |
| 2026-10-05 | Visual system and navigation pattern go to Claude Design | Visual iteration against a style reference (a prior stylized CV) suits a design tool better. Tokens come back here as CSS custom properties. |
| 2026-10-05 | Site voice derived from a private "Nathan voice" skill | The skill was built from real Slack writing and stays private because its examples name colleagues and internal projects. A new public register was added for the site, and only those rules live here. |
| 2026-10-05 | AI tools that assess Nathan speak in a neutral third person | A first-person self-assessment reads as self-promotion and undercuts the job-fit tool's honesty. |
| 2026-10-05 | CV content in `content/cv.json` plus a small build step (reverses "no build step") | Edit mode needs to know where each piece of text lives, and the AI tools need the same facts as data. A tiny script, with no framework, keeps the output plain static HTML. |
| 2026-10-05 | Private `/admin/` tools behind Cloudflare Access | Edit mode and the résumé generator are for Nathan only. Access handles login at Cloudflare's edge, so there's no auth code or password to maintain. |
| 2026-10-05 | Edit mode commits to GitHub | Git stays the source of truth and history serves as undo. Edits deploy through the same pipeline as code. |
| 2026-10-05 | Access login via GitHub (1-month session), not email codes or custom authenticator-app codes | One click when already signed in, and GitHub's authenticator-app 2FA provides the second factor. Home-built authenticator-code auth would mean maintaining sessions, brute-force protection and recovery for the page that can rewrite the CV. |
| 2026-10-05 | Two locks on private routes: Cloudflare Access plus the Worker verifying the Access token | The code is public, so a single misconfigured rule shouldn't be enough to expose data. |
| 2026-10-05 | Claude Design handoff v1 imported to `design/handoff/`; its `cv.json` becomes `content/cv.json` | The design pass delivered tokens, components, navigation, page specs and canonical content. The handoff governs visuals; DESIGN.md governs principles, data and privacy. |
| 2026-10-05 | Cloudflare Access instead of the handoff's custom GitHub OAuth | Custom OAuth puts the allowlist check, sessions and every endpoint's guard in our own public code. One bug could let any GitHub user in to a system holding private data. Access keeps the designed sign-in card and loses only the custom wrong-account page. |
| 2026-10-05 | Admin UI under `/admin/` with shared templates, not in place on public routes | Public pages stay static files with no admin code, and the Worker doesn't have to decide per request which HTML to serve. |
| 2026-10-05 | Card IDs frozen; duplicated `anchorage-6/7` detail split | Position-based IDs would break under drag-to-reorder. A shared bullet could appear twice on a generated résumé. |
| 2026-10-05 | Build script with zero dependencies (Node built-ins only), run by `wrangler deploy` | Nothing to install or update, and the output stays plain HTML. The build fails on content mistakes (duplicate IDs, unknown tags, repeated bullets) before anything ships. |
| 2026-10-05 | `[Bracketed]` placeholders hidden on the live site; unbuilt features behind flags | The PDF résumé already points recruiters here, so the live site shouldn't show unfinished copy or a fit CTA that leads to a placeholder. |
| 2026-10-05 | "5e-compatible", not "D&D 5e", in the DPR description | Follows the brief's rule against using official branding. |
| 2026-10-05 | v1 reviewed on a preview branch before replacing "coming soon" | Going live is public. The `workers.dev` preview lets Nathan review it first. |
| 2026-10-05 | The Worker shares the build's templates and validation | Edit mode renders the real page from the draft, so what you edit is what ships. The same checks run at build time and on every draft save. |
| 2026-10-05 | Every edit saves the whole draft, then reloads the page | Simpler and harder to get wrong than syncing the page by hand. The cost is a quick reload per change. |
| 2026-10-05 | Access token verification extracted and unit-tested (forged, tampered, expired, wrong-audience, unsigned) | It's the lock that matters if an Access rule is ever misconfigured, and the code is public. |
| 2026-10-05 | Footer email button fixed (white on white) | Caught in an edit-mode screenshot. The footer link colour overrode the button's colour. |
| 2026-10-05 | Tab icon "Ruled N" (from a Claude Design pass): teal N over the maroon title rule | Echoes the rule under every page heading. Built from shapes, not a font, so it renders the same everywhere. The SVG follows the system's light/dark setting. Sources and spec in `design/icon/`. |
| 2026-10-05 | Name/URL removed from the header; CV rail made sticky, with the current section highlighted | Nathan's call after seeing it live. The hero already carries the name, and a sticky contents list helps on a long CV. Overrides the handoff's "not sticky". |
| 2026-10-05 | First-party cookieless analytics in D1, shown in a private dashboard | Only first-party data can show the visitor's network owner without cookies. Third-party tools (Plausible, PostHog, Clarity) can do neither, or need cookies and consent banners. Cloudflare Web Analytics can run alongside as a free cross-check. |
| 2026-10-05 | No IPs stored; daily-rotating anonymous visitor ID; 13-month retention | Location and network owner are derived at request time, so storing IPs adds risk and no insight. Keeps the site free of personal data (principle 9). |
| 2026-10-05 | Session replay and heatmaps deliberately left out | They record individuals, need consent banners and cut against the privacy-first pitch. Revisit only for tool pages, behind consent. |
| 2026-10-05 | Job-fit tool runs on an Anthropic API key, not the Claude Code subscription | A subscription is for personal use in Claude's apps. A public tool needs its own metered key with a spend limit. |
| 2026-10-05 | Claude Opus 5.5 for the job-fit tool (about 7 cents per run) | Honest fit reads are judgment-heavy, and resisting manipulation matters more than saving a few cents. The test set will check whether a cheaper model holds up. |
| 2026-10-05 | Honesty enforced in code as well as the prompt | Citations are checked against real card IDs, quotes come from the CV rather than the model, and unsupported matches are downgraded. A prompt alone can't guarantee this. |
| 2026-10-05 | Layered limits: per-minute and per-day per IP, a daily cap, a monthly budget with email alerts ($10 at first, $4 since; see below), and the Console spend limit | Any one layer can fail or be gamed, and the budget turns the worst case into a paused tool rather than a bill. IPs are counted without being stored. |
| 2026-10-05 | Pasted postings are stored and disclosed on the page | They're business documents, not personal data, and they show Nathan which roles were checked. |
| 2026-10-05 | Skill wordings reviewed and approved by Nathan (149 wordings across 42 skills); two new skill groups added | The generator can only swap in wordings Nathan approved, so ATS matching improves without inventing anything. Claims that imply more than the experience shows ("People management", bare "React", "W-8BEN") were left out deliberately. The new Product practice and Domain and regulatory skills are each backed by result cards or Nathan's confirmation. |
| 2026-10-05 | Job-fit accepts a link: Greenhouse, Lever and Ashby through their public APIs, other pages through schema.org data or page text; LinkedIn and Indeed refused | Recruiters usually have a link. The fetched text fills the box for review, so nothing is assessed unseen. Sites that forbid automated access get a paste-instead message. https only, no IPs or internal hosts, redirects re-checked, size and time limits, 10 fetches per minute per IP. |
| 2026-10-05 | In-app budget lowered to $4 while the Console holds $5 with no auto-reload | The tool's own cap must trip before the account runs dry, so visitors get a clear "paused" message instead of errors. |
| 2026-10-05 | Stable facts are computed by code or stated once, never inferred per request (prompt v3) | Tenure comes from the role dates (exact, monthly, cache-friendly) and a curated `facts` list in cv.json is citable as evidence. The model stops doing date arithmetic, which removes a whole class of errors. |
| 2026-10-05 | Job-fit read streams and is built for a 10-second skim (prompt v4) | Recruiters skim. Verdict and a summary of 30 words or fewer arrive first; at most 6 one-line requirements ("✓ Meets · requirement · evidence card") and 2 open questions follow. A small streaming-JSON parser renders each part as soon as it is complete. |
| 2026-10-05 | Temporary admin-only A/B mode: Opus 5.5 and Sonnet 5.5 side by side | Nathan judges quality on real postings with time and cost visible, before choosing the production model. The server refuses model selection for non-admins. |
| 2026-10-05 | Opus 5.5 stays the job-fit model; Sonnet comparison behind `JOBFIT_COMPARE` (off) | Nathan preferred Opus's reads. The flag makes a re-test a one-line change. |
| 2026-10-05 | Built with Claude Code (AI-assisted) | Scaffolding, README and deploy steps were produced in a Claude Code session, with dashboard steps done by hand. |
| 2026-10-06 | Résumé generator assembles approved building blocks; Claude only picks them | Tailoring that rewrites claims can drift from the truth. Claude returns a plan of block IDs; code assembles, checks every ID, fits the page, and scores keyword coverage against the untailored CV. New wordings come only through review, each approved by Nathan. The generator's code is private; DESIGN.md describes it. |
| 2026-10-06 | Job-fit calls to action switched on (`jobFitLive`) before the public test set | Nathan wanted the tool reachable while he refines it on real postings. The $4 monthly budget, per-IP limits and daily cap still protect spend. |
| 2026-10-06 | Crypto and Onboarding role views, with hand-picked cards (`upFrontCards`) | Both cut across the existing tags, so tags alone would pull in the wrong results. Views are now generated from `cv.views`, so adding one is a content change. |
| 2026-10-06 | Role views page is a carousel: one card in focus, neighbours scaled back, looping in both directions, with swipe, arrow buttons and keys, and name pills | Five views made a grid feel like a wall of text. The carousel is a progressive enhancement: without JavaScript (and in print) it is the same grid. No auto-rotation, and motion follows the visitor's reduced-motion setting. |
| 2026-10-06 | Word export written by hand (a small zip and XML writer) rather than a library | A résumé needs only paragraphs and bullet lists. About 150 lines with no dependency, tested by unzipping it in the tests and by opening it in Microsoft Word, which reports one page. |
| 2026-10-12 | Job-fit grades: Exceeds, Meets, Close, Stretch or Gap, with a line on how each shortfall could be closed | Meets/Partly/Gap was too coarse: it put adjacent experience and no experience in the same bucket. Five levels, plus a grounded way to close each gap, tell the reader more. Code still enforces honesty: anything above Stretch needs a verified citation, and quotes are the CV's own words. |
| 2026-10-12 | Per-application ref codes removed | A code on a printed résumé reads as tracking and breaks when someone types the URL. Refs are kept only for clickable links Nathan controls (LinkedIn, GitHub). |
| 2026-10-12 | The job-fit read can say "Limited fit" | A tool that can only say yes is not believable. When most core must-haves are gaps, the verdict says so plainly. |
| 2026-10-12 | Job-fit daily cap lowered to 20 runs | 100 runs a day could cost more than the whole monthly budget, so one day of abuse would switch the tool off for the month. |
| 2026-10-14 | Visitor budget raised to $10 and counted on visitors' runs only; the owner's own AI use gets a separate $20 budget | One shared $4 budget let admin use (mostly testing) pause the public tool mid-month. Splitting them means the owner's use can't switch the tool off for visitors, and each still has its own cap and alerts. The Console spend limit remains the backstop. |
| 2026-10-12 | Content-Security-Policy added; the one inline script is allowed by its hash | Locks scripts, frames and connections to known origins. A test fails if the inline script changes without its hash. The job-fit settings moved to a JSON data block, which never executes. |
| 2026-10-12 | CI runs the tests and the build on every push and pull request | The deploy already ran the build; tests now run before anything is merged. |
| 2026-10-12 | Turnstile on the job-fit form; `/api/collect` rate-limited; the analytics salt cached per isolate | Turnstile stops scripted runs before they cost anything. The beacon endpoint only checked Origin, which a script can fake. Caching the salt saves two database calls per beacon. |
| 2026-10-12 | Private tools moved to a separate private repo, joined by a service binding; this repo restarted with a clean history | The public repo is portfolio evidence and doesn't need to carry Nathan's private tooling. The private Worker handles `/admin/*` and `/api/admin/*`, has no public route, and still checks the Access token itself. It uses this repo as a package, so templates, content and validation stay in one place. Both Workers share one D1 database, each with its own migration history. |
| 2026-10-14 | DPR calculator ported from Nathan's Python app as exact math in the browser, not a simulation | The same build always gets the same answer, and it's fast enough to recalculate as you type. Checked against the Python simulation's results: hit chances match exactly, averages within its margin of error (`tests/dpr.test.mjs`). |
| 2026-10-14 | DPR calculator is a standalone themed page (`/tools/dpr/app/`) behind a site-styled landing page, not an iframe | The site refuses to be framed (`frame-ancestors 'none'`), and the fantasy styling would fight the CV's design system. A separate page lets it go all the way. |
| 2026-10-14 | House rules (exploding dice, bigger dice against Large targets) left out of the public calculator | Results should match standard 5e rules. Rerolls and minimum die results stay: both are standard Great Weapon Fighting variants. |
| 2026-10-14 | Visitors can save fighter presets for everyone | Nathan's call. Public by design, and the save dialog says so first. Saves pass Turnstile, a 3-a-minute burst limit, 10 a day per visitor (hashed, like the job-fit tool), 100 a day site-wide and 2,000 stored. The same `normalizeFighter()` validates in the browser and the Worker, so only short names and bounded numbers are stored. Nathan hides a preset with `UPDATE dpr_presets SET hidden = 1 WHERE id = …`; `DPR_SAVING_ENABLED` switches saving off. |
| 2026-10-14 | The calculator's lettering is Sanguine Eye, Nathan's own typeface; numbers fall back to Georgia | The font has letters and basic punctuation only, by choice. Served from `public/assets/fonts/`. |
